name: Miscegenation
overview: Scripture presents miscegenation as a serious matter, beginning with Abraham's clear command not to take wives from the Canaanite nations, a directive reiterated to Jacob by Isaac to preserve the covenantal purity of God's people. The example of Esau marrying Hittite women, which caused grief to his parents, underscores the spiritual dangers associated with such unions. Moses further warns Israel against making covenants or marrying the daughters of the inhabitants of the land to prevent idolatry and spiritual unfaithfulness, emphasizing the protective and holy reasons behind this prohibition.
